rule: Aerobic benchmark: 30-min TT threshold pace 420 s/mi (7:00/mi), described as 'supporting ~3:16 marathon (Riegel)'.
summary: This is a goal-derived stepping stone, not a population norm, and none was found; keep it as a coach target. The Riegel claim in its note is contradicted: in 2,303 recreational runners, Riegel was well calibrated up to the half marathon but predicted marathon times at least 10 minutes too fast for half of runners. A 7:00/mi threshold therefore likely supports a marathon slower than 3:16. Self-paced running time trials carry about 2-2.7% test-retest error. Proposed: Keep 420 s/mi as a coach stepping stone, but replace the note 'supports ~3:16 (Riegel)' with 'Riegel overestimates marathon ability (often by 10+ min, Vickers 2016); the marathon projection comes from goal_progress using long-run and mileage data'. Possibly wrong if: the athlete's own half-to-full conversion matches Riegel.

sources.note: Vickers 2016: Riegel underestimates marathon time by 10 min or more for half of recreational runners; models using prior races and mileage do better.
5-km time-trial typical error 2.0% CV in trained male runners.
60-min treadmill time trial CV 2.7% in trained runners.
